title: Four Scandinavian Capitals and Norway in a Nutshell: Helsinki, Stockholm, Oslo, the Fjords, Bergen and Copenhagen

tagline: Four capitals, a night on the Baltic and Norway's most famous fjord journey

intro: Scandinavia's highlights in a week: Helsinki, an overnight cruise ferry into the Stockholm archipelago, Oslo's sculpture park and fjord, the famous Norway in a Nutshell route by train and boat, Bergen's wooden wharf and Copenhagen. We built this from our older brochure and corrected the Norway part: it slept in Geilo after reaching Myrdal, but Geilo lies before Myrdal on the line. You now sleep in Flåm, which splits the fjord journey into two easy days. Oslo's Viking Ship Museum is closed for rebuilding until about 2027.

best_time: May to September. Fjord boats and the Flåm Railway run all year, but summer has the most departures and the longest light.
seasons: Long light days (midnight sun in the Arctic from mid-May to late July), 15 to 22°C, all fjord boats and trains running.
Fewer crowds, cooler, and some mountain roads open late or close early.
Short days and snow; northern lights in the Arctic, Christmas markets in the capitals.

faqs.q: Can we see more of Stockholm?
faqs.a: Yes. Add a night in Stockholm (9 days), or take our Royal Capitals version: 2 nights each in Stockholm, Oslo and Copenhagen with a night in Gothenburg, all by train.
One Schengen visa covers all four countries; apply at the consulate of the country with the most nights.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

faqs.q: Is there support while we travel?
faqs.a: Yes. You have our 24/7 travel desk on +91 97148 59797 and +91 98242 21400 and a WhatsApp group with your consultant for the whole trip.

good_to_know.title: Hotel deposit
good_to_know.text: Use a credit card for the deposit or pre-authorisation at check-in, never a forex or debit card. Forex cards cannot hold funds, many hotels refuse them, and a credit-card hold is released faster.

good_to_know.title: Cards and cash
good_to_know.text: On card machines, always choose to pay in the local currency (euros in Finland, Swedish, Norwegian and Danish kronor elsewhere), never in INR. Scandinavia is almost cashless: cards and phone payments work everywhere, even for toilets and market stalls. You need little or no cash.

good_to_know.title: Pickpockets
good_to_know.text: Busy stations, trams and squares are pickpocket hotspots. Keep passports in the hotel safe, carry a copy, and wear your bag in front in crowds.

good_to_know.title: Plugs, water and meal times
good_to_know.text: Plugs are the two round-pin type C and F at 230 volts (Switzerland uses type J; a type C plug fits). Tap water is safe to drink. Lunch is about 12:00 to 14:00 and dinner from about 18:30.

emergency: Embassy of India, Adolf Fredriks Kyrkogata 12, Stockholm
dining_intro: Every city on this route has vegetarian and vegan restaurants and several Indian restaurants. In small fjord and Arctic towns choice is limited, so we send your dietary brief ahead to every hotel and ship.
dining_avoid: Soups, sauces, risottos and even some vegetable dishes are often made with meat or fish stock, and many cheeses use animal rennet. Show the food card and ask before ordering.
food_card: We are strict vegetarians (Jain). No meat, fish, seafood or eggs. No onion, garlic, potato, carrot or any root vegetables. No meat or fish stock. Thank you.
